name: Silas
summary: A leader and prophet among the believers who carried the apostles' letter to Antioch. He became Paul's companion, sang with him in prison at midnight, and helped spread the word through Macedonia.

key_moments.title: Sent with the Letter
key_moments.description: The apostles and elders chose Silas and Judas, leading men among the believers, to take their letter to Antioch. Being prophets, they encouraged and strengthened the believers there with many words.

key_moments.title: Chosen by Paul
key_moments.description: After Paul and Barnabas parted, Paul chose Silas, and the believers sent them off, commending them to God's grace. They travelled through Syria and Cilicia, strengthening the churches.

key_moments.title: Sings in Prison at Midnight
key_moments.description: After Paul cast a spirit out of a fortune-telling girl, her masters had Paul and Silas beaten and thrown into prison. At midnight the two prayed and sang praises to God, and after an earthquake the jailer and his whole household believed.

key_moments.title: Sent Away to Berea
key_moments.description: The believers sent Paul and Silas away by night to Berea, where many received the word eagerly. When trouble followed and Paul had to leave, Silas and Timotheus stayed on, and later they were told to join him at Athens.
